summary: The Ensuring Lasting Smiles Act requires group health plans and individual and group health insurance issuers to provide coverage for inpatient and outpatient care related to congenital anomalies or birth defects that primarily impact the appearance or function of the eyes, ears, teeth, mouth, or jaw. This includes medically necessary diagnosis, treatment, reconstructive services, and related dental or orthodontic support. General cosmetic surgery performed without a medical determination of a birth defect or anomaly is excluded from this mandate. The legislation also instructs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to study and report to Congress on network adequacy and patient out-of-pocket costs by December 31, 2027.

affected_groups.effect: Gain guaranteed health insurance coverage for medically necessary inpatient and outpatient treatments, reconstructive services, and related dental or orthodontic support.
affected_groups.group: Individuals with congenital anomalies or birth defects impacting eyes, ears, teeth, mouth, or jaw

affected_groups.effect: Must update coverage policies, cost-sharing structures, and plan documents to include mandated treatments and provide required notices to participants starting January 1, 2026.
affected_groups.group: Group health plans and health insurance issuers

key_provisions: Mandates group health plans and health insurance issuers to cover inpatient and outpatient items and services for congenital anomalies or birth defects primarily impacting the eyes, ears, teeth, mouth, or jaw.
Requires coverage to include medical necessities determined by a treating physician, such as restorative services, missing or abnormal body part treatments, and complications.
Includes adjunctive dental, orthodontic, or prosthodontic support from birth until medical or surgical treatment is completed, overriding standard plan exclusions on dental services.
Applies cost-sharing requirements to this mandated coverage that are no more restrictive than those applied to substantially all other medical and surgical benefits.
Excludes routine cosmetic surgery performed merely to improve appearance or self-esteem without a medical determination of a birth defect.
Requires health plans and issuers to provide participant and beneficiary notice regarding this required coverage starting no later than January 1, 2026.
Directs the Department of Health and Human Services to conduct a study and submit a report to Congress by December 31, 2027, evaluating provider networks and out-of-pocket cost changes.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Ensuring Lasting Smiles Act requires group health plans and individual and group health insurance issuers to provide coverage for inpatient and outpatient care related to congenital anomalies or birth defects that primarily impact the appearance or function of the eyes, ears, teeth, mouth, or jaw. This includes medically necessary diagnosis, treatment, reconstructive services, and related dental or orthodontic support. General cosmetic surgery performed without a medical determination of a birth defect or anomaly is excluded from this mandate. The legislation also instructs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to study and report to Congress on network adequacy and patient out-of-pocket costs by December 31, 2027.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a federal insurance coverage mandate for specific birth defects and congenital anomalies across group health plans and health insurance markets. It shifts financial responsibility for specialized reconstructive, dental, and surgical treatments onto health plans and changes compliance obligations for insurance providers starting in plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.
